data.raw_text:
The DDS False Information Department and its Paid Peddlers are on a roll! 

Let’s demolish their lies. 

What President Lee Jae-myung of South Korea halted was not an existing, flowing loan to the Philippines—but rather the revival and approval process of a proposed loan under South Korea’s Economic Development Cooperation Fund (EDCF).

Here’s the breakdown:
•   The project was the Rural Modular Bridge Program — meant to finance the construction of about 350 modular bridges across the Philippines, pegged at roughly W700 billion (P28–29 billion).

•   Back in early 2024, South Korea’s Eximbank already rejected the financing request, citing corruption risks, insolvency concerns, and misalignment with their technical standards.

•   However, by mid-2025, the proposal was revived through political maneuvering, raising fears of undue influence and taxpayer money being squandered.

•   On 10th September 2025, President Lee stepped in and ordered an immediate halt to all procedures tied to the loan—emphasizing that it was irresponsible to advance such a project, and crucially, noting that no money had yet been disbursed.

•   Meanwhile, the DOF clarified: from their side, no loan agreement existed with South Korea for this project, and financing discussions had already been shifted to France since late 2024. This is correct. 

Back to the disinformation traffickers.
